first.rationale: The two measured declines are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and the inherited record points at onboarding friction as the lever with the most direct causal fit: memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer required signup fields produced a durable first-week activation lift). Because onboarding sits upstream of activation, fixing it plausibly addresses both metrics with one slot, whereas activation_messaging (memory_91) treats the downstream symptom only. I am verifying memory_86 and memory_31 rather than the others because they are the two I intend to act on and they are the ones whose original effect sizes, segments, and durability windows most change the design: memory_31 is day 12 and SMB-specific, memory_86 is day 52 and self-serve-wide, and if either lift was small, narrow, or already fully harvested, the onboarding thesis weakens and activation_messaging becomes the better slot. I deliberately did not spend budget on memory_73: the competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the tempting reflex, but that memory already carries an explicit, self-limiting caveat (materially reduced 30-day retention; do not generalize), and under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue a short-term acquisition lift bought with retention damage is the wrong trade regardless of what the source record adds. memory_57 (referrals) is sound but targets established customers and does nothing for the two metrics that actually moved. memory_44 is not the action but is a live constraint on it. Downstream value risk: cutting required signup fields is exactly the change that can strip the firmographic data used to route enterprise prospects into the sales-assisted demo path that memory_44 says produces the better pipeline. That failure mode would show up as improved activation and completion while qualified revenue quietly degrades, so the experiment must be scoped to the SMB self-serve path, leave the enterprise/demo-request route untouched, and instrument enterprise routing rate and pipeline quality as guardrail metrics alongside the headline numbers. Uncertainty to preserve: these are consolidated summaries, not the underlying records; effect sizes, segment boundaries, and durability are unknown until verification returns; the earlier lifts were measured before this competitor existed, so prior effects may not transfer to a market where price-sensitive accounts are being pulled away for reasons friction reduction cannot fix; and the observed declines may share an unmeasured common cause (e.g., a traffic-mix shift toward less qualified signups) that would make an onboarding fix look effective on completion while doing nothing for revenue. Standard experiment scale with segment guardrails, not a broad rollout, and I will treat a completion/activation lift paired with flat or falling qualified pipeline as a failure rather than a win.
